comments.author: @LifewaysTravel
comments.text: Only about 4,000 people call St. John home, and life here is so different from what most of us imagine! 🇻🇮 Thank you for watching and exploring this beautiful island with us! ❤ Had you ever heard of St. John before watching this documentary? Let us know in the comments! 👇

comments.author: @UnseenOutlands
comments.text: I never realized how much daily life on St. John depends on ferry schedules. If someone works on St. Thomas or needs to travel for an appointment, what happens when bad weather cancels the ferry or they miss the last boat home? Is that something locals regularly plan around?

comments.author: @thompsonstewart7816
comments.text: People see the beaches and think it's pure luxury, but anyone who's lived here knows the real daily workout is checking the cistern water level and praying WAPA doesn't cut the power again!

replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text: That’s exactly the kind of everyday reality most visitors never see. ❤️ The beaches may look like paradise, but keeping an eye on cistern levels and dealing with power outages can be a real part of island life. Thanks for adding that firsthand perspective and showing what life beyond the postcard can actually feel like. 🇻🇮

comments.text: The fact that there's no airport and everyone relies on the ferry just to commute, shop, or get medical care makes you realize how isolated island life really is.

comments.author: @Lovingbird90
comments.text: What a beautiful paradise, keep your island, you don’t know how blessed your are, take care of those beautiful islands. Don’t move, make it better for your people.

replies.author: @LifewaysTravel
replies.text: Beautifully said. ❤️ St. John is more than just a beautiful place, it’s home to people with deep roots, memories, and community ties. Hopefully the island can keep its character while creating even better opportunities for the people who call it home. Thanks for sharing such a heartfelt message. 🇻🇮

comments.author: @travelintolifeus
comments.text: St. John looks like the kind of place that reminds you what really matters in life. Just 4,000 people surrounded by turquoise water, beautiful hills, and nature. I wonder if living in such a small community makes neighbors feel more like family.
